segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Mary Magdalene stayed behind at the tomb, weeping. When she was asked why she was crying, all she had was one answer.

segments.speaker: woman
segments.text: They have taken away my Lord, and I know not where they have laid him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: She had lost him once already. Now it felt like she had lost even the place where he lay.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: She turned and saw a man standing there.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Why are you crying? he asked her. Who is it you're looking for? She did not know the voice yet. Through the tears, she could not even see his face.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Thinking he was the gardener, she pleaded with him.

segments.speaker: woman
segments.text: Sir, if thou have borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Sir, if you carried him off, just tell me where you put him, and I will go and get him. She was a woman offering to carry a grown man's body home by herself. That is how much she loved him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said one word. Her name.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Mary. And she answered him — Rabboni. It means Master, in her own language, the word she had always called him. And instantly she knew. Grief flipped to joy in a single heartbeat — he was alive, and he had come looking for HER, by name.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended to my Father: but go to my brethren, and say unto them, I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my God, and your God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Don't hold on to me yet, he told her — I haven't gone up to my Father. Go to my brothers and tell them I'm going to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God. He gave her the message, and he sent her to carry it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The first person to see the risen Lord, and the first preacher of the resurrection, was a weeping woman he called by name.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He knows your name — and he speaks it even in your grief. Listen for it.
